title: Scene structure, transforms and the missing monitor arm

scenes.title: A visible housing is not the whole assembly

cues.text: The missing monitor arm began as a diagnosis problem, before it became a geometry problem.
The agent first focused on blank display surfaces and raised controls, then later identified the keyboard drawer as the clearest omission.
The user corrected that assessment: the right monitor arm was missing, and the left side supplied the reference.
The subsequent repair belongs to that clarified request. The earlier mistaken conclusion remains part of the execution history.

scenes.title: Objects, geometry and organization are different

cues.text: An imported Blender scene contains object instances, mesh datablocks, parents and collections. Each relationship answers a different question.
An object carries placement and other state; its mesh datablock supplies geometry, and multiple objects can refer to the same data.
The repair explicitly copies both the object and its mesh data, creating an independently editable right-side copy.
A collection organizes those copies and records metadata. That collection does not create a mechanical joint.
The earlier twenty-four manual-linked viewport annotations identified parts, but labels alone did not rig either support.

scenes.title: Mirror the world transform around a datum

cues.text: The V06 builder selects three named left-arm mesh objects: the support volume, outer arm and inner inset.
It builds a reflection matrix that negates the world X coordinate and adds a translation called mirror sum.
In one dimension, the mapping is X prime equals mirror sum minus X. The mirror plane is halfway along that sum.
Applying the matrix to each source world matrix reflects both placement and orientation, so the chosen datum directly controls the result.

scenes.title: A symmetric copy can still be misplaced

cues.text: The user later reported that the new right arm was not correctly placed.
The retained V06 source combines outer X edges; the V08 correction instead uses the centres of the two monitor-side world ranges.
It subtracts the old mirror sum from the new one, then shifts the right-arm copies by that difference.
The saved V08 report records a movement of about twenty-six point seven millimetres. A plausible mirror was not enough to establish the correct placement.

scenes.title: Bake the reflected copy without claiming closed geometry

cues.text: Before baking the corrected arm, the script makes another mesh copy if the data has multiple users.
It applies the captured world matrix to the mesh data and resets the object matrix to identity.
It then updates the data and flips polygon winding for the reflected copy.
Those operations address the transformed copy and its surface orientation. They do not fill the open arm surfaces or establish fabrication-ready geometry.

scenes.title: Change a parent while preserving the current pose

cues.text: Parenting changes the transform relationship, so assigning a parent can change an object’s visible placement.
The parent-keep-world helper updates the view layer and copies the object’s current world matrix.
It assigns the new parent, restores that captured world matrix, and updates evaluation again.
The goal is to preserve the current pose while establishing the hierarchy that future parent motion will drive.

scenes.title: Remove unrelated children from the moving group

cues.text: The imported hierarchy also attached unrelated desk meshes beneath some of the intended wing owners.
If those children were carried into the new motion hierarchy, a wing rotation could move parts of the desk.
The script captures each such child’s world matrix, clears its parent and restores its world placement.
Only the selected wing parts and support pieces are then assigned to the intended hinge stages.

scenes.title: State what the hinge coordinates actually mean

cues.text: The requested repair called for lower and upper hinge axes based on reference geometry.
The retained script describes its actual pivot positions as approximate centres of rounded silhouettes on the imported side arm.
It creates two empty objects with arrows, using coordinates in the source model’s inch-sized unit system.
Those controls define a visual rig. They are not surveyed bearing coordinates, and the code explicitly labels the result as not fabrication-ready.
The lower hinge is linked to the imported root when that root is present.
The upper hinge becomes a child of the lower stage, with its initial world position preserved.
Both arm assemblies follow the lower hinge; the selected display wing follows the upper hinge.
A change at the lower stage therefore carries the upper stage with it, while the upper stage adds its own relative rotation.
The script names four poses: open, intermediate, folded and locked, at frames one, forty, eighty and one hundred.
It sets lower and upper X rotations in radians, then inserts rotation keyframes for both controls.
Illustrative lock objects are shown at the final pose by keying their viewport and render visibility.
A pose named locked and a visible wire loop do not demonstrate a functioning latch, bearing forces or a dynamic simulation.

scenes.title: Trace the TimelineMarker failure and repair

cues.text: One recorded V08 attempt tried to store a custom angle property on a timeline marker.
Blender rejected the assignment because that type did not support the attempted ID properties.
The historical patch removed the unsupported assignment and retained the marker creation call with its label and frame.
The rig then reran successfully. Being a Blender RNA structure does not mean that every type accepts arbitrary custom properties.

scenes.title: Evaluate a pose before measuring its envelope

cues.text: The source sets each pose frame and updates the view layer before collecting transformed mesh bounds.
The recorded development also encountered hinge empties evaluated at the origin before the pivot and dependency updates were corrected.
The saved report gives a folded height of about one hundred eighty-two millimetres, compared with the recorded reference value of one hundred eighty-one.
The width and depth still exceeded the reference values. Agreement on one envelope dimension did not validate the complete assembly.

scenes.title: Keep visual comparison inside its evidence boundary

cues.text: The mechanics audit found that visual symmetry alone had not supplied pivots, grouped motion or closed arm surfaces.
The reference-view fit helped compare visible screens, encoders and supports, but one illustration could not establish hidden geometry or folding behaviour.
Later sampled poses and limited overlap tests answered narrower questions than continuous clearance or full mechanical validation.
Keep the geometry, parent chain, chosen datums, unit assumptions and tested pose set attached to each claim.

scenes.title: Carry a structured assembly into measurement

cues.text: The missing-arm case moved from a corrected diagnosis to copied geometry, a corrected datum and a two-stage visual hierarchy.
Objects, mesh data, collections and parents remained separate parts of that explanation.
The marker failure has a recorded repair, while the approximate pivots and open surfaces retain their stated limits.
The next chapter follows the measurement problem: connecting photographs and drawings to model coordinates through explicit assumptions.
